item.title: Turkey Central Bank Ups Year-End Inflation Forecast to 28%
item.description: Turkey’s central bank abandoned its below-consensus inflation call and moved its year-end forecast to 28%, closer to market expectations.

item.title: Flipkart Founder’s Navi Said to Hire Banks for $315 Million IPO
item.description: Fintech startup Navi Ltd. is preparing to formally kick off the process for an initial public offering in India, seeking to raise as much as 30 billion rupees ($314 million), according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Nigerian Central Bank Widens Access to Open Market Operations
item.description: Nigeria’s central bank broadened participation in Open Market Operations, allowing all eligible investors including individuals, corporates and non-bank financial institutions to participate in the purchase and trading of the securities.

item.title: Australia’s Top Gold Miner Spurns Elliott Push to Revamp Board
item.description: Northern Star Resources Ltd., Australia’s largest gold miner, has rejected activist investor Elliott Investment Management LP’s calls to overhaul the company’s board.

item.title: Deutsche Bank’s DWS Backs Insurer, Eyes Private Markets Mandate
item.description: DWS Group is partnering with life insurance consolidator Frankfurter Leben as the asset manager owned by Deutsche Bank AG seeks to access the industry’s vast capital pools.

item.title: UK Economy Weathers Early Months of Iran War With 0.4% Growth
item.description: Britain’s economy weathered the initial months of the Iran war, as sunny weather and World Cup football kept consumers spending in the second quarter.

item.title: Lenovo Shares Surge 22% After Revenue Beat Renews AI Optimism
item.description: Shares of Lenovo Group Ltd surged after the Chinese computer maker reported a 43% increase in quarterly revenue, beating analyst estimates by a wide margin and reinforcing optimism around AI-driven demand.

item.title: Adyen Boosts Revenue Outlook as Clients Process More Payments
item.description: Adyen NV raised its net revenue growth outlook for the year on the back of growing demand for the Dutch payments firm’s services from both new and existing clients.

item.title: YMTC Passes Kioxia in NAND Shipments for First Time, Report Says
item.description: China’s Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. edged out Japan’s Kioxia Holdings Corp. for the first time in flash memory shipments during the June quarter, a sign that Chinese chipmakers are benefiting from AI-driven shortages.

item.title: Modi Faces Pressure as Parliament Disrupted by Protest Fallout
item.description: India’s monsoon session of Parliament was dominated by opposition disruptions as lawmakers demanded Home Minister Amit Shah’s resignation over police action against widespread student protests, adding to pressure on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government.

item.title: Thyssenkrupp Raises Outlook Slightly on Steel, Warship Gains
item.description: Thyssenkrupp AG raised the low end of its full-year profit guidance as it reported strength at its steel and naval divisions despite a challenging global industrial environment.

item.title: Japan’s Government Is Said to Support Faster BOJ Rate Hike
item.description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government is supportive of a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan, with the next move likely either in September or October, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Bank of Korea Makes First Gold-Linked Investment in 13 Years
item.description: South Korea’s central bank bought gold-related assets for the first time in 13 years, joining global reserve managers turning to the precious metal as a hedge against geopolitical and economic uncertainty.

item.title: India’s RBI Turns Upbeat as Worst of Iran War Shock Recedes
item.description: Five months after the Iran war raised fears of an inflation spike and an economic downturn, Indian officials are sounding more confident as the worst of those concerns have so far failed to materialize.

item.title: Meta Says It’s Shut Down 750,000 Under-16 Accounts in Australia
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. says it has removed access to more than 750,000 Instagram and Facebook accounts in Australia believed to belong to people under 16 since it began complying with the country’s landmark youth social media ban last year.

item.title: Aluminum Extends Fall From Seven-Week High as Supply Fears Ease
item.description: Aluminum fell for a second day after one of the Middle East’s biggest smelters announced plans to restore production earlier than expected, blunting fears over a growing shortage of the metal.

item.title: Vietnam Banks Laden With $77 Billion Funding Gap Face Pressure to Lend Even More
item.description: Vietnam’s central bank has warned that demand for capital is outstripping lenders’ ability to mobilize funds, just as the government urges them to ramp up credit to support its double-digit growth target.

item.title: Shein Is Said to Consider Aug. 28 for Hong Kong Trading Debut
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd. plans to start taking investor orders for its long-awaited Hong Kong initial public offering as soon as Aug. 20 and debut in the city around Aug. 28, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Korea Steps Up Home Supply Push as President Faces Discontent
item.description: South Korea raised its cap on household debt growth and pledged more homes in the Greater Seoul area, stepping up efforts to contain a relentless housing rally that’s becoming a political liability for President Lee Jae Myung.

item.title: Tata Investors Turn Focus to Succession, Strategy as Chairman Set to Step Down
item.description: Shares of Tata Group firms lost about $4.5 billion in combined market value on Wednesday.

item.title: Prabowo Picks Insiders for Top Indonesia Central Bank Posts
item.description: President Prabowo Subianto nominated three senior Bank Indonesia officials to fill the central bank’s top leadership positions, reinforcing expectations of policy continuity after he picked Destry Damayanti as the sole candidate for governor.

item.title: Trump Enlists Private Sector to Boost Cyber-Offensive Arsenal
item.description: The US government is partnering with private-sector firms to launch cyber attacks abroad, expanding the scope of national security operations that until now have been largely conducted by government agencies.

item.title: Housing Market Jitters Grip Australia Banks on Cautious Outlook
item.description: Banks revealed the extent of the depressed housing market sentiment in Australia this week, dragging down their share prices and underscoring the pressure on profitability.

item.title: China’s Coal-to-Chemicals Push Pays Off With Record Profits
item.description: China’s decade-plus quest to replace oil with coal in chemicals production is paying off for industry leader Ningxia Baofeng Energy Group Co., which pulled in record profits as crude prices soared due to the Middle East War.

item.title: Anthropic Said in Talks to Buy Startup Decart for $6 Billion
item.description: Anthropic PBC is in talks to buy the artificial intelligence startup Decart AI for about $6 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Australia Home Price Drop Adds to Restrictive Stance: RBA’s Kent
item.description: Australia’s softening housing market is contributing to financial conditions potentially being a bit more restrictive than otherwise, the Reserve Bank’s Assistant Governor Chris Kent said at an event.
